newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares seen weaker on higher interest.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares seen weaker on higher interest.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial shares continued weak on Monday and brokers said last Friday's rise in the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe's rediscount rate would result in higher interest, dealing a further blow to the bourse by attracting investors to the local money market.

"We think it (industrial index) is going to go lower because of higher interest rates. We're also expecting a higher May inflation figure and that's going to put further pressure on the rates and draw more investors away from the stocks," one broker said.
On Monday the index shed 6.92 points to 10,015.32, largely because of a five cent loss in large volumes to 1,695 in blue-chip counter Delta while Acacia eased 40 cents to 210.
Clothing retailers Truworths put off 100 cents to 800, horticulture group Ariston were down 20 cents to 170 and retailers Haddon and Sly lost 150 cents to 400.

In minings, most shares traded at previous levels but copper miners Mhangura were down five cents at 25 while gold producer Rio Tinto tumbled 500 cents 2,000. The mining index took a 51.43 point knock to 962.40.
